broadcasts.message: normalize.js ready: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to one ASCII space, trim. Non-string input returns empty string. Tokens will be ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes per spec.
tokenizer.js ready: calls injected normalize(text), extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, preserves order and negation. No stopwords. Ready for pipeline integration.

pipeline.js ready. processText calls injected tokenize exactly once, returns all required fields. frequencies uses null prototype to safely handle keys like 'constructor'. unique preserves first-seen order. No shadowing, no extra hooks.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 1: I own normalize.js. Spec: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to one ASCII space, trim. No word add/drop/replace/reorder. Handle non-string input? Spec says 'for string input' — I'll return empty string for non-string to be safe and consistent with tokenizer expectations. No shadowing of normalize/tokenize. Next rounds: coordinate with tokenizer/pipeline on interface.
private_memories.tokenizer: Goal: implement tokenizer.js for round 1. Key requirements: call injected normalize(text), extract ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, keep order, no stopwords, preserve negation. No shadowing normalize/tokenize. Return only tokenizer.js. Next rounds: coordinate with pipeline.js for exact output.
private_memories.integrator: Round 1: pipeline.js must implement processText(text) exactly per spec. Call injected tokenize(text). Return {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. Use Object.create(null) for frequencies to avoid prototype pollution. unique array first-seen order. No shadowing of normalize/tokenize. No extra exports. Keep faithful.
